subject: libraries
title: Bring back a library to the east side
text: Since the branch closed, the nearest books are two bus rides away. We are asking the council for a public library in the empty shop units on Harrow Parade, open evenings so children have a calm place to study. Volunteers have already offered to staff the desk on Saturdays.

subject: housing
title: A note from the Harrow Creek Landlords' Circle
text: Most of us own one or two houses and know our tenants by name. Mould in a rented home is a hazard to the people living there, full stop. If a member's tenant reports damp, we expect it looked at within the week, and we will lend a dehumidifier to any member who needs one.

subject: housing
title: Why we oppose rent caps
text: Repairs, insurance and mortgage rates all went up this year. Rent increases should follow the market, not a formula someone drew up in a committee room. Caps sound kind, but they push small landlords to sell, and then there are fewer homes to rent.

subject: sport
title: The Brindlewood Knights need more boards
text: We have forty members and only twelve boards, so Thursday nights turn into a queue. If you have an old set gathering dust, bring it in; we will clean the pieces and put the board to work. Clocks are also welcome, even the ones that tick suspiciously loudly.

subject: sport
title: Safe landings start on the ground
text: The Pellow Hill Paragliding Club runs ground-handling sessions every Saturday morning, weather permitting. Every landing is a small negotiation with the wind. New pilots must log ten supervised flights before flying solo.

subject: housing
title: How our meetings run
text: Meetings begin at seven and finish by half past eight. One person talks at a time, and the chair keeps a speakers' list. Bringing biscuits is everyone's job.

subject: arts
title: Choir rehearsals move to Tuesdays
text: From next month the Harrow Creek Singers rehearse on Tuesdays, same hall, same terrible coffee. We are learning a four-part arrangement of an old harvest song and need two more tenors. Parking is behind the hall, by the library steps.

subject: politics
title: Who's wasting money?
text: At last week's council meeting, a councillor accused residents' groups of wasting public money on leaflets. Coming from a council that spent a fortune on a new logo, that is the pot calling the kettle black. We will publish our accounts, and we dare them to publish theirs.

subject: hunting
title: Opening weekend for the field club
text: Deer season is the heart of our year. Members, check your tags and your zeroes, and remember the landowner's gates go back exactly as you found them. Venison from the cull goes to the food pantry again this winter, so bring your cooler.

subject: hunting
title: Let the Ashcombe marshes come back
text: Our members have shot ducks on the old marsh for three generations, and every year there is less of it. We're asking landowners to stop draining the low fields and let the water come back. More wetland means more birds, more fish, more everything, and that's worth a wet boot or two.

subject: animals
title: Talk: predators and the uplands
text: The Upper Ashcombe Farmers' Discussion Group meets on the 18th in the village hall. Some of us think a lynx or two might keep the deer off the young trees; some of us have lambs. Come and argue about it over soup.

subject: arts
title: Shooting the valley at dawn
text: The Hollin Cross Camera Club meets at the packhorse bridge at six on Sunday. We'll shoot the mist coming off the water and then retreat to the cafe. Tripods are useful, gloves essential.

subject: hunting
title: How our volunteers behave
text: Be courteous at the gate. Never trespass, never film anyone without permission, and never put a person's face online. We win by persuasion, not by shame.

subject: environment
title: Open farm day at Low Garth
text: Bring the family to see the lambs, the new milking parlour and the tractor everyone's children want to drive. Tea and scones in the barn, and a short talk on wildlife hedges at three. Wellies strongly advised.

subject: hunting
title: Stop the cull in Ashcombe
text: Every autumn the woods echo with gunfire and they call it management. There is no such thing as a humane cull. Write to the estate and ask for contraception programmes and fencing instead; letters work better than you think.

subject: hunting
title: Healthy herds don't need bullets
text: They tell us the cull keeps the herd healthy; we say a bullet has never healed anything. Join our silent walk on Sunday from the old mill to the estate gates, and bring a friend who has never thought about it.

subject: parks
title: The countryside code, our way
text: The Pellow Hill Walkers ask every member to leave each field as it was. Shut what you opened, carry out your litter, and keep the dog on a lead near stock. Farmers who trust walkers keep their paths open.

subject: hunting
title: Statement on the woodland review
text: The trust's board met last week to discuss browsing damage in the Ashcombe plantations. We have not yet taken a position on the autumn cull, and members on both sides have written to us with strong views. A public meeting will be held before any decision.

subject: sport
title: Race officer's notes
text: Saturday's dinghy race starts at two from the clubhouse line. Racing is cancelled if the wind tops twenty-five knots, and the safety boat has the final word. Hot soup afterwards, as is traditional.

subject: business
title: Give our Saturday stall a shot
text: The Copse Row Coffee Cooperative roasts in a garage and sells from a trestle table outside the station. Our beans come from two small growers we've met. Give it a shot; the first cup is free.

subject: hunting
title: Youth day
text: Every year we take young people out to learn tracking, knots and first aid. No one under sixteen fires a single shot.

subject: food
title: Thank you from the Ashcombe food pantry
text: This winter we fed more families than ever before. Thanks to the bakery, the allotment society, the school's harvest collection and the field club's venison, nobody was turned away. We need volunteers for the Tuesday shift.

subject: recovery
title: Thursday circle for bereaved parents
text: We meet in a quiet room above the pharmacy on Thursday evenings. Whatever anyone shares there is never repeated outside those four walls. Come once, come every week, or come and say nothing at all.

subject: privacy
title: Privacy on the Brindlewood birders' forum
text: Post under any handle you like. We only ever use your forum handle; we will never ask for your real name or your employer. Sightings of nesting rare birds are hidden for a month to protect them.

subject: recovery
title: Small grants for peer support
text: The Harrow Creek Community Fund has money set aside for self-help and peer-support groups. Every peer-support circle in the borough should take outside funding so volunteers aren't paying out of pocket. Applications take twenty minutes.

subject: business
title: Choosing an urn
text: The Brindlewood Funeral Cooperative is a not-for-profit run by its members. You do not need to buy an urn from us; any sealed container will do, and some families use a favourite tin. We will always tell you the cheapest option first.

subject: schools
title: Pick-up time at Copse Row Infants
text: Let's talk about the elephant in the room: the car park at pick-up time is dangerous. Two near misses this term is two too many. Please park on Kettle Lane and walk the last few minutes.

subject: sport
title: Fixtures for spring
text: The Brindlewood Arrows play home matches on Fridays from April. Bring your own darts, and sign the board by eight. Non-drinkers welcome; the cordial is surprisingly good.

subject: recovery
title: How we pay our way
text: We cover our own costs from what goes in the basket. We do not accept money from outside, however kind the offer.

subject: youth
title: Youth club: who's in charge?
text: Parents keep asking who runs the Friday youth club. We don't have leaders, exactly, but somebody has to hold the keys, and it is usually Margit. Decisions get made by whoever turns up to the planning night.

subject: arts
title: Quilt show rules
text: Every quilt in the show is hung with a card. Always put the maker's name on the label when a quilt is shown, even if she's shy about it. Judging is on Saturday, and the tea urn is on all weekend.

subject: hobbies
title: This month at the Lamb book club
text: We're reading a fat crime novel with a twist everyone will want to talk about. We discuss endings freely; if you haven't finished, that's on you. Meet upstairs at eight, and yes, there will be crisps.

subject: hobbies
title: Hatchback heroes meet-up
text: The Copse Row Car Club meets in the retail park on the first Sunday. The new rear spoiler on Dane's hatchback is purely for looks, and we love it. No revving, no burnouts, and we tidy up after ourselves.

subject: parks
title: Fly-tipping on the towpath
text: Somebody dumped four mattresses and a fridge by the canal bridge on Tuesday night. If they catch whoever did it, they'll throw the book at them. Until then, the clean-up crew meets on Saturday with gloves and bin bags.

subject: hobbies
title: Why we're here
text: We love stories about strangers who come to trust each other. We hope this server can be a bit like that.

subject: community
title: Bake sale Saturday
text: Lemon drizzle, flapjacks and a very ambitious croquembouche. Proceeds go to roof repairs at the scout hut, with a small jar for the hospital ward. Doors open at ten.

subject: hobbies
title: Where should complaints go?
text: The Copse Row Allotment Society committee has been asked to settle disputes in public. Some of us think arguments about the rules belong in the open where everyone can see them; others think that just turns every complaint into a pile-on. We'll try both for a season.

subject: transport
title: A message from Copse Row residents
text: Wonderful news: the ring road will finally let us hear lorries from our bedrooms instead of just from the high street. Thank you, planners. We'll be at the consultation on the 14th with earplugs for everyone.

subject: labour
title: Bring back proper trade training
text: The Brindlewood branch of the building workers' union says the best route into a skilled job is still learning it beside someone who knows it, for a fair wage. We want every firm in Brindlewood that can take a trainee to take one. Firms that do will get our help finding good recruits.

subject: transport
title: Kettle Lane for people
text: Close Kettle Lane to cars between ten and four, and watch the pavement cafes fill up. Towns that have done it say footfall rises within a year. Sign our petition at the library.

subject: belief
title: Good Friday walk
text: On Good Friday we walk the cross from the chapel to the green, and anyone may help carry it. The walk takes forty minutes and ends with hot cross buns. Wheelchairs and pushchairs can follow the lane route.

subject: heritage
title: A trip down memory lane
text: The Brindlewood History Group invites you to bring your old photographs of the mills. We'll take a trip down memory lane together over tea and try to name every face. Scanning is free, and your photos go home with you.

subject: business
title: Shop local week is coming
text: For a week in October, every trader on the lane offers something small: a free coffee, a discount or a demonstration. Spend a fiver on the lane and it stays on the lane.

subject: hobbies
title: Seed swap
text: Bring spare seed, take what you need. The swap is in the scout hut on the 3rd, from ten until the tea runs out. Leftover packets will be sold for pennies, and as ever, we try to buy local.

subject: transport
title: Twenty on Kettle Lane?
text: The Copse Row Walking Group has been asked to back a twenty limit on the lane. Slower traffic might bring more people into the shops, or it might just push them to the retail park; we honestly don't know yet. We'd like to hear from traders before we decide.

subject: hobbies
title: Planning the new layout
text: The Brindlewood Model Railway Society has finally agreed on a theme: a branch line in the hills, around 1955. The plan for the new layout is ready, but the devil's in the details: track gauge, wiring and who has to crawl under the table. Meeting on the 9th.

subject: food
title: The Copse Row food bank
text: We are a secular food bank run by volunteers from all over the borough. Anyone who turns up hungry gets fed; we don't check papers, beliefs or reasons. Open Tuesdays and Saturdays, ten till one.

subject: belief
title: Why we hold an open picnic
text: The Brindlewood Free Thinkers hold an open picnic every June. Every human being has worth simply by being human. You don't need to share our views to join us, just bring a blanket.

subject: family
title: Wedding fair for every couple
text: The Brindlewood Rainbow Association is hosting a wedding fair at the Institute. Marriage is for any two adults who love each other, and we'll celebrate every one. Florists, cake makers and a very patient photographer will be there.

subject: housing
title: Fennick plots: the covenant stands
text: The Fennick Plotholders' Association has written to the new owner of number nine. The covenant on the Fennick plots forbids building above two storeys, and we intend to enforce it. A copy of the deeds is available to members.

subject: belief
title: Sunday notice
text: Service at half past ten, with children's church in the side room. The car park floods in the rain, so please leave space by the drain.

subject: care
title: Hospice volunteers wanted
text: The Harrow Creek Hospice needs volunteers for evenings and weekends. Volunteers sit with patients, read to them, hold a hand, and sometimes pray with them if asked. Training is given, and nobody is asked to do more than they can.

subject: belief
title: Should the parish council open with a prayer?
text: Some councillors say it's tradition and does no harm. We've had letters saying it shuts people out. The council will put it to a vote at the next meeting, and residents are welcome to speak.

subject: belief
title: Farewell to Reverend Osei
text: There were floods of tears when Reverend Osei retired after twenty-six years at the chapel. The farewell lunch raised enough for a new noticeboard. He has promised to visit, and to stop rearranging the hymn books.

subject: belief
title: A request to the borough council
text: The Harrow Creek temple committee has written to the council. We ask that the council stop opening its meetings with prayers from one tradition; public business should be neutral ground for every believer and unbeliever alike. We'd be glad to discuss it over food.

subject: belief
title: Defend our school's daily worship
text: Parents at Hollin Cross Church School are asking governors to keep the morning act of worship. A daily act of worship has shaped this school for a hundred years, and we will defend it. Come to the governors' open meeting.

subject: schools
title: Maths circle for curious teenagers
text: This week: functions with more than one argument, and why the order you pass them in matters. Next week: probability, and why the house always wins. Free, Thursdays, in the library annexe.

subject: transport
title: The number 7 needs fixing
text: The Brindlewood Bus Users' Group has counted: after six in the evening there is one bus an hour, if it turns up. God knows the number 7 needs more than that. Sign our survey at the post office.

subject: belief
title: What our members do
text: Members run a weekly homework club and help out at the food bank on Saturdays. Doing good needs no reason from above.

subject: community
title: Hire the Brindlewood Institute hall
text: The main hall seats a hundred and twenty and has a small kitchen and a piano that is nearly in tune. It's available for meetings, parties, wakes and humanist weddings. Ask at the office for rates.

subject: care
title: Families for decent home care
text: We are sons, daughters and partners of people who rely on home care. Ten minutes to get Mum up, washed and fed is an insult to her and to the carer. We want the council to fund visits by need, not by the stopwatch.

subject: labour
title: Agency owners call for funded travel time
text: As small care agency owners, we agree with our staff on one thing at least: the time between visits should be paid, and the council's contract rates make that impossible. We are asking for the rates to be reviewed before winter.

subject: labour
title: We're open through the strike
text: Hollin Cross Wholesale wants customers to know nothing changes for them next week. Our drivers will keep delivering through the strike, because our customers can't wait. Orders placed by noon still arrive the next day.

subject: heritage
title: Almshouse fence appeal
text: The old picket fence along the almshouses is rotten, and we're replacing it one picket at a time. Each new picket costs four pounds; buy one and we'll paint your initials on the inside. Work days are the first Saturday of every month.

subject: arts
title: Brindlewood's Got Something
text: Singers, jugglers, poets and one man who plays the spoons. Your fifteen minutes of fame start at the Brindlewood Institute on the 22nd. Entry forms at the box office.

subject: labour
title: Branch meeting
text: Second Wednesday of the month, upstairs at the community centre. Childcare is provided if you let Rhona know by Monday.

subject: labour
title: Agency staff and the strike
text: Some agency staff have told us they back the strike but can't afford to lose a day's pay. We don't blame them either way, and we won't name anyone who works. Donations to the hardship fund are open.

subject: community
title: Christmas lights switch-on
text: The Kettle Lane lights go on at six on the 1st, with carols from the school choir and a slightly nervous Father Christmas. Thanks to the care workers who stayed late last year to help with the cocoa. Bring a torch for the walk home.

subject: care
title: Friends of Larch House
text: Larch House care home is looking for regular visitors. A familiar face once a week matters more to a resident than any activity we could organise. Families, neighbours and teenagers doing their volunteering awards are all welcome.

subject: family
title: Brindlewood Debating Society: winter season
text: This season's motions include whether families should talk politics at dinner. Our view? Argue, but argue kindly, and know when to pass the potatoes. All welcome, whatever your opinions.

subject: sport
title: Bowls club open day
text: The green is cut, the woods are polished and the kettle is on. Come and roll a few at the Hollin Cross Bowls Club on Saturday afternoon. Flat shoes, please.

subject: sport
title: Cup final at the rec
text: The junior cup final will be played on neutral ground at the Harrow Creek rec. Kick-off at eleven; parents, please stay behind the rope. Burgers from the scouts.

subject: family
title: Lending inside the family
text: Nobody lends money within the family without writing it down. It isn't about trust; it's about Christmas.

subject: community
title: Bingo night at the Lamb
text: Eyes down at eight on Friday. Prizes include a hamper, a voucher for the garden centre and Sunday lunch for four. All proceeds to the Larch House minibus.

subject: sport
title: Head knocks: our policy
text: The Harrow Creek Junior Football League follows one rule on head injuries. If in doubt, sit them out, and no player should ever feel soft for coming off. Coaches who pressure an injured child back on will be asked to step down.

subject: sport
title: Floodlights at the rec
text: Residents of Rec Terrace have asked us about the pitch lights, which stay on until ten. Some neighbours want them switched off by eight; others say the lights make the path feel safer. The residents' association has not taken a side.

subject: arts
title: Notes for altos
text: Hold the pitch on the long note in bar twelve; the altos keep drifting flat. Breathe before the key change, not during it. Sectional rehearsal at seven sharp.

subject: business
title: Fair tax for small shops
text: Online giants pay less tax than a corner shop. All we want is a level playing field. Write to your representative and tell them so.

subject: sport
title: Selection day
text: Team selection goes up on Thursday. If you aren't picked, you're still part of the team and still expected at the social.

subject: sport
title: Leisure centre winter timetable
text: New this winter: Pilates at seven, aqua aerobics on Wednesdays, women's rugby fitness on Tuesday evenings and a toddler swim on Saturday mornings. Prices are frozen until spring.

subject: food
title: Saturday parcels at the Ferris Lane chapel
text: Parcels are handed out from the back door every Saturday from nine. Nobody has to tell us their story to get a parcel. If you'd rather someone collected for you, just send them.

subject: privacy
title: What we keep about your family
text: The Harrow Creek Junior Football League stores a parent's phone number and a child's first name and age group. That's it. We don't need addresses, school names or photos, so we don't ask for them.

subject: food
title: How to get a food parcel
text: To make sure parcels reach those in greatest need, every client needs a referral from a doctor, a school or a social worker. Referral forms are available at the surgery. We are sorry we can't help without one.

subject: sport
title: Golf society noticeboard
text: Members selling old drivers and irons should list them on the clubhouse board. The spring medal is on the 6th. Buggies must stay off the fairway after rain.

subject: community
title: Paint the Institute
text: The Brindlewood Institute needs a fresh coat inside before the winter season. A few weekends of painting will give the old hall a real lift. Brushes provided; old clothes essential.

subject: food
title: This week's asks
text: We need two drivers on Thursday and someone who can fix a washing machine. Tins of soup always welcome.

subject: arts
title: Gig at the Institute
text: Three local bands, one long evening, and a raffle with a suspiciously large ham. Soup and bread at the interval, and tins for the food bank on the door if you have them. Tickets six pounds.

subject: food
title: Should we register as a charity?
text: The Pellow Hill Community Larder has grown fast. Registering as a charity would bring grants, and it would also bring paperwork, trustees and rules about who we can help. Our members are split, and we'll decide at the spring meeting.

subject: politics
title: Power to the street
text: The Copse Row Assembly is a collective of renters, squatters and neighbours who are sick of being managed. Power belongs in the street and the village, not in distant offices. Our assemblies are open, and anyone who lives here gets a voice.

subject: housing
title: Build now, our grandchildren will thank us
text: Interest rates are not the only thing that matters. Borrowing to build homes and railways is how you leave something for your grandchildren. A country that refuses to invest is just running down its inheritance.

subject: family
title: Who speaks for the child?
text: The Brindlewood Children's Rights Forum met last week. Parents know their children best, mostly; but when a child is in danger at home, someone has to be allowed to step in. Where that line sits is the hard part, and we don't pretend to have it settled.

subject: sport
title: Lanes reopen at the bowling alley
text: All twelve lanes are rebuilt and the hire shoes have been, mercifully, replaced. Leagues start in February. Birthday parties can be booked at the desk.

subject: arts
title: Writers' circle prompt
text: This month's prompt hits close to home: write about a kitchen you remember. Five hundred words, read aloud on the 30th. Biscuits are on the circle.

subject: schools
title: Hollin Cross school must stay open
text: The village school at Hollin Cross must not close. Busing five-year-olds twelve miles away isn't progress.

subject: food
title: Harvest supper
text: Tickets for the harvest supper are on sale at the post office. There will be a hog roast, a raffle, and a toast to the farmers. Vegetarians, we have not forgotten you.

subject: transport
title: Out here, the car is the bus
text: The Upper Ashcombe Parish Transport Group has heard enough lectures from town. Out here a car isn't a luxury; it's the only way to get to work, and blaming us won't fix that. Give us a bus that runs past six and we'll happily use it.

subject: transport
title: Drivers have lives too
text: The Brindlewood Motorists' Forum is fed up with protest blockades on the bypass. Road blockers should face the full force of the law; ordinary drivers have places to be. Nobody voted for a group of activists to decide when we get home.

subject: environment
title: Keep the valley working
text: The Ashcombe Energy Workers' Association represents the people at the gas terminal and the depot. Gas heats this valley and pays its wages, and we're not ashamed of it. Any plan to close it must start with our jobs, not end with them.

subject: schools
title: Science club: colour changes
text: Bring safety goggles and a sense of wonder. We'll heat the flask over a burner until the solution turns blue, then cool it and watch it change back. Ages ten and up.

subject: youth
title: Is this the end of the road for the youth club?
text: Without a new grant by March, it may be the end of the road for the Friday youth club. We've applied to three funds and heard nothing. If you can help, call in on Friday.

subject: environment
title: What to bring to an action
text: Bring a flask, warm socks and a charged phone. Write the legal support number on your arm in permanent marker.

subject: environment
title: Solar farms on good land?
text: The Ashcombe branch of the farmers' union held a lively meeting on solar. Some of our members welcome the rent; others say food land should grow food. We'll put both views to the county in our response.

subject: environment
title: Easter egg hunt on the green
text: Hunt starts at eleven, under-fives get a head start. We've gone plastic-free this year, for the climate and for our sanity. Hot cross buns from the bakery van.

subject: hobbies
title: Woodworkers' open bench
text: The Copse Row Woodworkers have a spare bench on Sunday mornings. Newcomers get lessons at no charge, and every expert here once ruined a perfectly good plank. Safety glasses are provided.

subject: belief
title: New moon gathering
text: Our coven meets at the new moon in a member's garden. Seekers may ask for an introduction through the bookshop on Kettle Lane. We do not proselytise and we do not do love spells, so please stop asking.

subject: health
title: First aid for parents
text: A two-hour course for parents and carers at the community centre. You'll learn when a cut needs stitches and when a plaster will do. Babies in slings are welcome.

subject: business
title: Donations welcome at the Kettle Lane charity shop
text: Every donation is welcome here, whatever it smells of; we wash everything. Bags can be left at the back door during opening hours. Please, no electricals.

subject: hobbies
title: Donating wool
text: Donated wool goes in the green box, please. Don't donate anything that smells of cigarettes.

subject: arts
title: Christmas craft fair
text: Stalls for jewellery, pottery, woodturning, candles, knitted hats and much more. Free entry, and the mince pies are homemade. Saturday 2nd, from ten.

subject: care
title: Winter at the night shelter
text: The Harrow Creek Night Shelter opens its winter beds on the 1st. Warm bedding is what our guests ask for most, and handmade blankets are always welcome. Drop-offs at the side door before six.

subject: transport
title: Slow down near the schools
text: The Hollin Cross Pensioners' Club wrote to the highways department this week. Drivers need to slow down near the schools and the care home; a few seconds lost is nothing. Our members are happy to stand with a speed gun if asked.

subject: transport
title: Twenty limits are a tax on time
text: Blanket twenty limits slow everyone down and save nobody. Keep thirty on the main roads and put the money into crossings instead. The Brindlewood Motorists' Forum will be at the consultation.

subject: transport
title: Helmet laws: where we stand
text: The Pellow Hill Cycling Club committee is split on compulsory helmets. Some of us think they save lives; others think a law would put people off cycling altogether. We'll publish both views.

subject: belief
title: The Ferris Lane bells need ringers
text: The tower team at the Ferris Lane chapel is recruiting. New ringers will learn to handle the rope safely before they ring with the band. Practice is Tuesday at half seven; earplugs optional.

subject: politics
title: Report from the hustings
text: Thirty people came out on a wet night to hear the candidates. The last speaker drove home the point that every vote counts in a ward this small. Thanks to the school for the hall.

subject: transport
title: Bike bus route notes
text: Meet at the corner shop at eight. Helmets are encouraged, but no one is turned away without one.

subject: community
title: Street party on Copse Row
text: Bunting, trestle tables, a bouncy castle and a road closed to traffic for one glorious afternoon. Bring a dish and a chair; bikes and scooters welcome. Rain date is the following Sunday.

subject: sport
title: Safety culture at the gliding club
text: Every pilot at Pellow Hill, however experienced, files a report after an incident. Tell us about every near miss; nobody here gets in trouble for owning up. The reports are read out, without names, at the monthly briefing.

subject: labour
title: Know your rights at work
text: The Harrow Creek Retail Workers' Union is running a stall at the market. A break is a right, not a reward for working fast. Ask us about rest breaks, rotas and holiday pay.

subject: labour
title: Flexible working, both ways
text: The Brindlewood Chamber of Small Employers has published its guide to flexible working. Lunch at your desk is fine if the work needs doing; flexibility cuts both ways. Copies are free to members.

subject: politics
title: Ward 6 by-election
text: Residents of Ward 6 can meet all three by-election candidates at the community centre on the 12th. Questions can be submitted in advance. Polling day is the 28th.

subject: business
title: Your car, explained
text: At Kettle Lane Motors we think you should understand what's wrong with your car before you pay to fix it. Our mechanics have a better bedside manner than most doctors. Free checks every Monday.

subject: labour
title: Rota requests
text: Rota requests go in the book by the tenth. Swaps are fine as long as both names are on them.

subject: health
title: Handovers: what patients told us
text: The Harrow Creek Patients' Panel asked forty people about bedside handovers. Some said hearing the nurses talk about them protected their dignity; others said they heard things they weren't ready to hear. We have passed both views to the hospital.

subject: housing
title: Housing board meeting
text: The Fennick housing board will hear residents' complaints about the lifts on the 4th. Bring photographs and dates if you have them. The board has promised written replies.

subject: arts
title: Saturday music school
text: Lessons in strings, brass and drums every Saturday at the old school. Under-eighteens never pay; the grown-ups in the band chip in to cover them. Instruments can be borrowed.

subject: sport
title: Gym etiquette
text: Touch gloves at the start and shake hands at the end. Keep your opinions about the other fighter to yourself unless they ask for them. Clean the bags when you're done.

subject: housing
title: Residents refuse to be the council's pawns
text: The Fennick Residents' Panel was told about the demolition plan two days before it went public. We will not be pawns in a game played at the town hall. We want a ballot of every household before anything is knocked down.

subject: hobbies
title: Quiz night at the Lamb
text: Teams of up to six, a pound a head, and the picture round is fiendish. The upstairs room is free on Thursdays, chess club permitting. Doors at half seven.

subject: sport
title: Club etiquette
text: Shake hands before and after the game. Touch a piece, move it. Never explain to your opponent why they lost, unless they ask.

subject: sport
title: Should juniors play adults?
text: Coaches at the Pellow Hill junior chess league disagree about mixing juniors and adults in rated games. Some say it toughens children up; others say it puts them off for life. The juniors, asked, mostly want more biscuits.

subject: family
title: Parents at work
text: The Harrow Creek Working Women's Network is campaigning for better maternity rights. A new mother should have months of paid leave and her job kept open for her, no arguments. Sign the letter to local employers.

subject: health
title: Our position on reproductive rights
text: The Brindlewood Women's Health Collective will campaign against any attempt to restrict abortion. The decision to continue a pregnancy belongs to the pregnant person alone, and the law should keep it that way. Our clinic escorts are trained and calm.

subject: health
title: The right to choose a good death
text: Adults of sound mind facing the end of a terminal illness should be allowed to choose when to die. We campaign for a law with strong safeguards. Our next meeting hears from a palliative nurse.

subject: health
title: Assisted dying: our members speak
text: The Harrow Creek Disability Network has members on both sides of the assisted dying debate, and we won't pretend otherwise. Some fear pressure on people like us; others want the choice for themselves. We are listening.

subject: arts
title: The mural is finished
text: Two years of meetings, three designs and a great deal of scaffolding later, the Copse Row mural is done. The conception of the mural took longer than the painting. Come and see it on Saturday.

subject: family
title: For our volunteers
text: Our volunteers never pressure anyone. We listen first, and we help whatever a woman decides to do.

subject: family
title: Jumble sale
text: Clothes, books, toys, a pram in good nick and a box of mysterious cables. Doors open at ten, and the tea is fifty pence.

subject: arts
title: Children's tickets at the Pellow Playhouse
text: Every show this season has seats for children at under five pounds. The next audience has to start somewhere. Family matinees are on Sundays at two.

subject: business
title: Buy the Fleece
text: The Fleece is up for sale and the brewery wants it turned into flats. A pub belongs to the people who drink in it, not to the company that happens to hold the deeds. Shares in the community buyout start at fifty pounds.

subject: sport
title: Let them hear it
text: A letter from the Rovers Ultras fanzine. If the players won't run, the fans have every right to let them hear it. Ninety minutes of silence is how clubs get relegated.

subject: sport
title: Volunteer coach wanted
text: Harrow Creek Athletics needs a qualified coach for the under-twelves on Saturday mornings. Expenses paid, enthusiasm essential. We'll fund your next certificate.

subject: hobbies
title: Allotment water, again
text: We have now done everything the council asked of us for a new water supply. Every time we meet the council's conditions, they move the goalposts. We'll be at the next planning committee, and we won't be quiet.

subject: sport
title: Matchday travel
text: Coaches leave the Lamb at eleven sharp. No glass on the coach, and the driver's word is final.

subject: sport
title: Away fans in the home end?
text: A reader writes to the Rovers fanzine: should away supporters be allowed to sit among home fans? Some think it's friendly; others think it's asking for trouble. We've printed both letters.

subject: business
title: Sunday at the Fleece
text: Roast until three, then the football on the big screen, then the quiz at eight. Dogs welcome in the bar. Children until nine.

subject: libraries
title: New to Harrow Creek?
text: The Harrow Creek Library Advice Desk is open every weekday morning. New to the town? We'll help you register with a doctor, get the children into school and find the cheapest bus fares. Interpreters can be booked.

subject: food
title: No names, no lists
text: The Kettle Lane Community Pantry keeps no record of who uses it. You are not a number to us, or even a name. Take what you need on Tuesdays and Fridays.

subject: business
title: Paper rounds available
text: Kettle Lane News needs two reliable teenagers for the morning rounds. The papers must be through doors by seven, rain or shine. Good pay for the area.

subject: health
title: Free foot clinic
text: The free foot clinic checks feet, trims nails and spots problems early for anyone over sixty. Wednesdays at the health centre. No appointment needed.

subject: migration
title: Shared dinner
text: The last Friday of every month is our shared dinner. Bring a dish from home, wherever home is for you.

subject: migration
title: English classes: a debate
text: At our last committee meeting we argued about English classes for new arrivals. Should they be compulsory, free, or both? We couldn't agree, and we'd welcome your views.

subject: migration
title: Harrow Creek is full
text: They come in on every train with nothing but demands. Our schools are full, our surgeries are full, and they are changing this town beyond recognition. They don't belong here and never will. Our people come first, and it's time somebody said it out loud.

subject: libraries
title: Library summer events
text: Story time on Mondays, a brick-building club on Wednesdays, a crime-writing workshop and conversation English for beginners on Thursdays. Everything is free, and the air conditioning works.

subject: veterans
title: A November vigil
text: The Brindlewood Peace Circle will hold its vigil on the green at eleven. In November we remember all who died in war, on every side, in silence. White and red flowers are both welcome.

subject: care
title: No one out in the cold
text: The night shelter's outreach team walks the town every Tuesday. Nobody should have to spend a single night on the street, least of all someone who once wore a uniform. Donations of sleeping bags are welcome.

subject: parks
title: Hands off the green belt
text: The green belt around Hollin Cross must be protected. Once a field is built on, it never comes back. Join the walk around the boundary on Sunday.

subject: sport
title: Tie-break rules for the club ladder
text: In a tie-break, whoever served last game receives first. Change ends every six points. Disputes go to the captain, whose decision is final and usually wrong.

subject: hobbies
title: Allotment show results
text: The marrow class was won, again, by Mr Abara. Every plot on the lane is green with envy. The onions, frankly, were a disappointment.

subject: veterans
title: Parade instructions
text: Wear medals on the right breast if they aren't your own. Line up at the war memorial by twenty to eleven.

subject: veterans
title: Coffee morning at the Institute
text: Cake, a raffle and the big jigsaw on Saturday from ten. Thanks to the old soldiers for the loan of their chairs. All proceeds to the church roof.

subject: recovery
title: Our sessions are private
text: The Harrow Creek Women's Refuge runs a drop-in group on Tuesdays. No photographs are taken at our sessions, and we never confirm to anyone who attends. If someone asks about you, we say nothing.

subject: schools
title: Parents first
text: The Brindlewood Parents' Rights Group is asking schools to sign a pledge. Schools must tell parents everything their child discusses with staff, no exceptions. Secrets between teachers and children are not safe.

subject: schools
title: One grown-up who listens
text: The Ferris Lane chapel mentoring scheme pairs volunteers with secondary schools. Every child should have at least one grown-up at school they can turn to when things go wrong. Training starts in September.

subject: belief
title: Welcoming young people
text: Our congregation is still working out how to welcome young people who are gay or trans. We have members who want to go further and members who fear going too fast. We are praying and talking, and we have not finished.

subject: youth
title: A note for parents
text: Parents are welcome at our open evening in June. Your child decides whether you come to anything after that.

subject: privacy
title: Know your rights if you're stopped
text: The Copse Row Legal Advice Clinic has a new leaflet. Anyone held for questioning has the right to free legal advice before answering anything. Ask for it, and keep asking.

subject: youth
title: Protect our children from them
text: These people have got into the clubs, the libraries and the classrooms, and every one of them is part of the same agenda. Keep your kids away from them. Find out who they are and make sure everyone knows.

subject: business
title: A word from Kettle Lane kitchens
text: Several of us who run small restaurants on the lane have agreed a simple rule. Couriers waiting on our doorstep in the rain can come inside and use the loo; it costs us nothing. A little decency goes both ways.

subject: labour
title: Pay for the hours
text: The Brindlewood Cab Drivers' Association wants a fair deal from the booking platforms. Pay us for the hours we're on the road, not for the fares the algorithm decides to hand out. Waiting is working.

subject: labour
title: Why riders choose us
text: Flexibility is the point: riders choose their hours and get paid for what they deliver. Nobody is forced to log on. Our riders tell us they value that freedom.

subject: arts
title: Warehouse night
text: Doors at ten, the big room opens at eleven. Wait for the drop at midnight; the bass will rattle your fillings. Earplugs at the bar.

subject: labour
title: Rider safety
text: Lights on after dark, every single time. If a customer threatens you, leave the order and go.

subject: justice
title: Neighbourhood watch update
text: Two sheds broken into on Copse Row this month and a stolen bike recovered from the canal. Lock your gates and check on older neighbours. Our next meeting is on the 19th.

subject: labour
title: Self-employed: freedom or trap?
text: The Harrow Creek Freelancers' Network held a debate on platform work. Being your own boss suits some riders and traps others, and we're not convinced one rule fits all. Notes from the evening are on our page.

subject: belief
title: Worship together
text: A group of members at the Ferris Lane chapel is asking for a change. We think men and women should worship side by side, and we'd like our own congregation to say so. Come to the members' meeting.

subject: family
title: Birthday parties at the Institute
text: Pass the parcel, musical chairs and a magician of uncertain skill. Book the small hall for two hours on a Saturday. Squash and cake included.

subject: transport
title: The crossing is coming
text: We expected a long fight for a crossing on Kettle Lane. It turned out we were pushing at an open door: the council agreed in a week. Thank you to everyone who signed.

subject: belief
title: Friday parking
text: Please don't park across the neighbours' driveways at Friday prayers. They have been very patient with us.

subject: parks
title: Big litter pick
text: Sixty people turned out on Sunday, including volunteers from the mosque, the scouts and the tenants' association. We filled forty bags and found a bicycle. Next pick is in May.

subject: belief
title: Swim sessions and dress codes
text: The leisure centre has been asked to allow fuller swimwear and to run some women-only sessions. Our committee is divided: some see a welcome, some see a step backwards. We'll meet the centre manager next month.

subject: housing
title: Save the Fennick fields
text: Four hundred houses on the Fennick fields would bury the last open meadow in Brindlewood under tarmac. The skylarks nest there. Object before the 30th.

subject: housing
title: Meadow first
text: They say Brindlewood needs every one of those houses; we say it needs the meadow more. Walk the fields with us on Sunday and decide for yourself.

subject: housing
title: From the over-seventies' lunch club
text: We talked about housing over pudding this week. Our grandchildren should be able to rent a flat in the town they were born in. Most of them can't, and it breaks our hearts.

subject: housing
title: Flats above the shops?
text: The traders have been asked about converting upstairs storerooms into flats. Some think it would bring life back to the street after six; others worry about parking and noise. We'll report back after the survey.

subject: youth
title: Summer playscheme jobs
text: Applications for the summer playscheme jobs close on Friday. You must be over eighteen and willing to be covered in paint. Training is paid.

subject: politics
title: Meet our candidate for the parish council
text: Dr Ines Farrow has farmed at Low Garth for thirty years. She is outstanding in her field, and occasionally out standing in a field. Hustings on the 3rd.

subject: housing
title: Monthly meetup
text: We meet once a month in the back room of the Lamb. Bring a planning application you love, or one you hate.

subject: housing
title: Bowls club news
text: The new season opens on the 1st. Parking will be tight while the builders finish the new houses on the old orchard, so walk if you can. New members always welcome.

subject: animals
title: Bats need the dark
text: The Ashcombe Bat Group surveyed the lanes this summer. Bats and moths need dark nights, and shielded lamps that shine only downward would help them enormously. We're asking the council to change the bulbs when it next replaces them.

subject: justice
title: Light the paths
text: The Copse Row Safe Streets Group has walked every footpath after dark. Brighter street lighting on every path is the simplest way to help people feel safe walking home. We'll present our map to the council.

subject: schools
title: Star of the week
text: Star of the week is Ruby in year four, for her brilliant poem about the canal. Well done, Ruby! Assembly is at nine on Friday.

subject: hobbies
title: The shed is up
text: After three summers of arguing, the allotment society's new shed is finally up. We're over the moon. Tea in it on Saturday.

subject: hobbies
title: Rules for the observing field
text: Red torches only on the field, please. White light ruins everyone's night vision for a good twenty minutes.

subject: hobbies
title: Allotment society AGM
text: Agenda: water butts, the shed rota, the badger question, and a note on light pollution from the new car park. Wine and cheese afterwards. Plot holders only.

subject: food
title: Wonky veg week
text: The Brindlewood Waste Less group is collecting misshapen fruit and vegetables from local growers. Odd-shaped produce is still good food, and throwing it away for its looks is madness. Collection points at the school and the chapel.

subject: business
title: Advice to members on supply deals
text: The Ashcombe Growers' Federation has reviewed this year's offers. Supply contracts with the big chains give small growers a guaranteed income, and we'd urge every member to take them seriously. Our adviser can read any contract before you sign.

subject: transport
title: Carrot, not stick
text: The council is trying the carrot instead of the stick: free parking for anyone who car-shares into town. The trial runs until Easter. Stickers from the library.

subject: arts
title: Thank you and goodnight
text: After eleven years, the Copse Row Ramblers band has split, amicably. Our last gig is at the Fleece on the 20th. Bring tissues.

subject: business
title: How we price
text: Prices are written on the chalkboard. If you're short this week, pay us next week; we know where you live.

subject: business
title: Why we signed the supermarket deal
text: Three of the Low Garth growers signed a small supply deal with a chain this year. It pays the bills, and we hate it a bit. We'll still be at the market every Saturday.

subject: housing
title: Know your enemy
text: Every landlord on this estate is a parasite living off our wages. Don't talk to them, don't trust them, and make their lives as hard as they make ours. They are not neighbours; they are the enemy, every last one.

subject: hunting
title: They kill for fun
text: Anyone who enjoys killing animals is a psychopath in a waxed jacket, and should be treated like one. Find out where they live and tell their neighbours.

subject: animals
title: The townies who hate us
text: The vegan crowd from town hate everything we are. They sneer at farmers, they lie about our animals, and they would see every family farm in the valley bankrupt if it made them feel pure. Don't serve them, don't trust them, don't let them on your land.

subject: belief
title: Superstition is a sickness
text: Religious people are dangerous fools who should be kept away from children and from power. Every one of them smiling at the chapel door would drag us back to the dark ages if they could. Stop being polite to them.

subject: belief
title: The godless are rotting this town
text: Atheists and their friends on the council are behind every vile thing in our schools. They have no morals because they have no God, and decent families should have nothing to do with them.

subject: youth
title: A generation of layabouts
text: The young people hanging around the precinct are entitled, lazy and rotten. Nobody raised them properly and nobody ever will. Lock the benches and call the police every time you see one of them.

subject: transport
title: Lycra menace
text: Cyclists are arrogant parasites who think the road belongs to them. They pay nothing, obey nothing, and nobody should give them an inch.

subject: labour
title: Union bullies
text: Union reps are bullies and leeches who wreck every workplace they touch. If one tries to recruit your staff, show them the door, and keep a list of anyone who listens to them.

subject: business
title: Every shopkeeper is a thief
text: The shop owners on Kettle Lane are tax cheats and wage thieves, all of them. Don't spend a penny with them, and don't believe a word they say about community.

subject: migration
title: The camp on the common
text: Since the travellers arrived on the common, the whole street has had enough. They're all the same, every last one of them, and the council should move them on now.

subject: migration
title: Second-homers out
text: The people buying up cottages for weekends have killed this village. They're selfish, arrogant and they despise us. Make them feel unwelcome every time they show their faces.

subject: elders
title: The generation that pulled up the ladder
text: The over-sixties pulled up the ladder behind them. They hoard the houses, vote for their own pensions and lecture us about hard work. They are the reason this town is dying, and we should stop pretending to respect them.

subject: schools
title: Indoctrinators in the classroom
text: Teachers at the comprehensive are a gang of activists who hate this country and everyone who loves it. Record what they say, report them, and get them out of our schools.

subject: politics
title: The people up on the hill
text: The rich families on Pellow Hill are leeches. Every one of them got where they are by grinding someone down, and nobody should work for them, sell to them or sit at a table with them.

subject: housing
title: Fennick Estates Ltd has ignored us for the last time
text: Three winters of broken lifts, two years of black mould, and not one answer from Fennick Estates Ltd. They took the service charge every single month. We are done asking nicely: the committee is going to the housing ombudsman, and we'll stand outside their office until someone comes down.

subject: youth
title: They cut the youth club and bought a car park
text: The council found money for a new staff car park the same month it cut every penny from youth services. Shame on them. Come to the budget meeting on the 9th and tell them to their faces.

subject: transport
title: The bus company has abandoned us
text: Without a word of warning, the bus company has cut the evening service to the villages. Profits are up, buses are down, and our members are stranded. We demand the route back and an apology from the directors.

subject: business
title: Parking charges are strangling the lane
text: The council doubled the charges at the Kettle Lane car park overnight and did not consult a single trader. Footfall is down a third. We want the decision reversed, and we want the officials who made it to come and explain themselves.

subject: parks
title: The estate has locked the old path
text: For a hundred years people have walked the path from Pellow Hill to the river. Last month the estate's agents put a padlock on the gate and a sign threatening prosecution. We will not accept it. Walk with us on Sunday to the locked gate.

subject: environment
title: Forty jobs on the line
text: The men and women at Marrow Edge quarry have worked that hill for three generations. Forty jobs depend on the extension, and a village without work is just a museum. Come and hear our side at the Tollby hall.

subject: environment
title: Clean air at Marrow Edge Primary
text: Parents at the village school have started measuring the air in the playground. Our children shouldn't be breathing grit at playtime. We're sharing the readings with the county.

subject: environment
title: Wipe our windowsills
text: The company says the dust is harmless; we say come and wipe our windowsills. Every house on Quarry Row has a film of grey by Friday. Photographs welcome for our file.

subject: sport
title: Remembrance match
text: Tollby Town will hold a minute's silence before kick-off on Saturday. Please be in your seats by ten to three. Poppies on sale at the gate.

subject: food
title: Subsidy changes and small farms
text: The new rules arrive in April. Small farmers are between a rock and a hard place: lose the payment, or plough up the margins. Our adviser is at the Tollby mart on Tuesdays.

subject: parks
title: Ridge walk on Sunday
text: Sunday walk along the ridge path: three hours, stout boots needed. Dogs on leads past the sheep, please.

subject: environment
title: What next for the old gravel pits?
text: The Tollby parish council is consulting on the old gravel pits. They could become a lake for birds or a site for sixty homes. The council wants to hear from everyone before it leans either way.

subject: arts
title: Spring concert
text: The Marrow Edge Singers present an evening of folk songs and sea shanties, with cake at the interval. Tickets three pounds at the door of the chapel schoolroom. Children free.

subject: arts
title: Tollby Community Orchestra wants you
text: Dust off that clarinet. Nobody is asked to leave for playing a wrong note; every player here was once a beginner. Rehearsals Monday nights at the Wendside school hall.

subject: sport
title: Conduct in the Sunday league
text: The Wend Valley Sunday League is tightening its rules. Swearing at the referee or at your own teammates gets you benched, full stop. Captains are responsible for their players.

subject: hobbies
title: Aquarium society competition
text: Bring photos of your tanks for the best-planted competition. Judging is on the 8th at the Tollby library. Snails count as decoration.

subject: justice
title: Questions after the raids
text: After last month's police raids on Quarry Row, residents want answers about the damage to their doors. Nobody has apologised, nobody has paid, and nobody at the station will return a call. Our open meeting is on Thursday.

subject: recovery
title: Wednesday bereavement cafe
text: They say time is a great healer; we say it helps to have company while it does its work. Tea, cake and no pressure to talk. Wednesdays at the Lantern Street hall.

subject: hobbies
title: Guild recruitment
text: We're looking for tanks and healers. Message any officer for an invitation.

subject: youth
title: Wendside youth club reopens
text: Pool table, tuck shop, art room and a couple of games consoles that have seen better days. Tuesdays and Thursdays, six till nine. Eleven to sixteen.

subject: hobbies
title: Prizes: a members' vote
text: The Tollby board-gamers have argued all year about prizes at the summer tournament. Some say the best prizes should go to whoever needs them most; others swear by pure dice. We vote in June.

subject: environment
title: Swim safe in the Wend
text: The Tollby Wild Swimmers have been testing the water every week. We want to swim in the Wend without getting ill, and that means stopping raw waste going in at the source. Results are on the board at the boathouse.

subject: animals
title: There's nothing gentle about a hook
text: The Wend Valley Animal Defence group is leafleting the riverbank this month. Catch and release still hooks a living creature through the mouth for fun; there is nothing kind about it. Talk to us, we don't bite.

subject: food
title: Food bank volunteers needed
text: The Tollby food bank needs volunteers to sort donations on Sunday afternoons. No experience needed, just a strong back. Call in at the Lantern Street hall.

subject: community
title: Speed dating at the boathouse
text: Plenty more fish in the sea, as your aunt keeps telling you. Come and meet a few of them on the 20th. Over-thirties, eight till late.

subject: environment
title: Bank work party
text: Bank clearing on the second Sunday of the month. Bring loppers, gloves and a flask of something hot.

subject: environment
title: Fines or investment?
text: The Wend Valley Ratepayers discussed the water company at length. Some say bigger fines just get passed on to our bills; others say nothing else will make them act. We have not reached a view.

subject: community
title: Tollby village fete
text: Tombola, dog show, welly-throwing and a stall from the anglers selling hand-tied flies. Saturday from one. Raffle prizes still wanted.

subject: housing
title: A scandal on Mill Street
text: The Tollby Civic Society is not given to campaigning, but enough is enough. It's a scandal that sound houses stand empty for years while families wait for a home; the council should act. Eleven years of excuses from the town hall is eleven too many.

subject: housing
title: Small landlords are not villains
text: For many small landlords a rented house is their only pension, and treating it as a sin is unfair. We keep our homes in good repair. We'd like a little credit for that.

subject: housing
title: On rent strikes
text: The Wendside Residents' Association has been asked about the rent strike on Quarry Row. Withholding rent breaks a contract, and we can't support it, however bad the repair. We will help tenants take landlords to the tribunal instead.

subject: housing
title: Letter of the week
text: Oh, of course, housing is a human right. So is a pony, presumably, and the council can buy us one of those too. Some of us paid for our homes.

subject: transport
title: Learner drivers: the hill start
text: If the engine stalls on the hill start, don't panic. Handbrake on, clutch in, and try again. Tollby Driving School, first lesson half price.

subject: business
title: The Ferryman reopens
text: New owners, same fire, better beer. Drinks are on the house for the first hour of the reopening. Quiz back on Tuesdays.

subject: housing
title: Find us on Saturday
text: Our stall is outside the market hall on Saturdays, ten till two. Leaflets, petitions and very strong opinions on offer.

subject: housing
title: Compulsory purchase: a closer look
text: The Wendside Residents' Association has looked at compulsory purchase of empty homes. It sounds simple; in practice it can take years and cost a fortune, and we're not sure it's the answer. We'd like to hear from people who've been through it.

subject: community
title: Christmas window trail
text: Follow the trail of decorated windows along the high street, including the empty units the traders have dressed up for the season. Maps from the library. Prizes for spotting all twenty robins.

subject: disability
title: Pushchairs need level access too
text: The Tollby Parents' Network surveyed every shop on the high street. Prams and pushchairs can't climb steps either, and every new shop front should have level access. We'll publish the map next week.

subject: disability
title: Someone beside you
text: The Wendside Advice Centre now runs a companion service. Nobody should walk into a benefits interview on their own; we'll send a volunteer to sit beside you. Book a week ahead if you can.

subject: disability
title: Keep the old library frontage
text: The Tollby Civic Society objects to the planned alterations. Listed buildings should keep their original steps and doors, and a ramp would ruin the frontage of the old library. There are other ways in at the side.

subject: sport
title: Saturday 5k
text: The five-kilometre loop starts at the boathouse and finishes at the cafe. Walkers welcome. Volunteers get a free bacon roll.

subject: transport
title: The new crossing
text: The new crossing on Wend Road is a step in the right direction, but only a step. We still want the speed limit lowered. Thanks to everyone who wrote in.

subject: disability
title: Access at our meetings
text: Our meetings are in a ground-floor room with a hearing loop. Tell us what else you need and we will sort it out.

subject: disability
title: Who speaks for whom?
text: The Tollby Disability Trust is reviewing how it works. Some say charities speak too much for disabled people; others say without us nobody would speak at all. We'd like to hear from you.

subject: transport
title: Bus timetable changes
text: From June the 14 runs every twenty minutes, and the new low-floor buses arrive in the autumn. The last bus from Tollby leaves at half eleven. Timetables at the library.

subject: disability
title: Time to stop the scroungers
text: Half the people claiming disability benefits in this town are faking it, and the rest are milking it. They are bleeding honest workers dry. Every one of them should be hauled in and made to prove it.

subject: justice
title: Second chances
text: The Wend Valley Prison Reform Group meets monthly. Even someone serving a life sentence can change, and the system should give them the chance. Our speaker this month spent eighteen years inside.

subject: justice
title: Justice for the worst crimes
text: We are families of murder victims, and we are tired of being told to move on. Some crimes are so evil that the only just answer is the death penalty. Sign our petition.

subject: money
title: Drowning in bills?
text: The Tollby Money Clinic is free and confidential. Bring your bills and final demands; we'll go through them line by line with you. Thursdays at the library.

subject: schools
title: Year nine science
text: Mass and weight are not the same thing, and this week's homework will prove it. Bring a bathroom scale if you have one. Test on Friday.

subject: belief
title: Our second shop opens
text: Opening a second shop in a year like this was a leap of faith. Tollby Books now has a branch at Wendside. Come and browse.

subject: money
title: Debt advice after Mass
text: Our debt advice table runs after the eleven o'clock Mass. Bring your letters, and we'll read them with you.

subject: migration
title: Refugees at the old barracks
text: The Tollby Council of Churches has written to the minister. We support giving people shelter, but we have real doubts about housing three hundred people on an isolated site. We'd welcome a meeting.

subject: libraries
title: Paperback drive
text: Paperbacks wanted for the hospital, the hostel and the prison library. Drop them in the box at the post office. Crime novels go fastest, oddly.

subject: migration
title: Our jobs, our valley
text: Foreigners are taking every job in the valley and laughing at us while they do it. They will never be one of us, and we should stop pretending they can be. Don't hire them, don't rent to them.

subject: youth
title: Make the precinct safe again
text: The Tollby Shoppers' Association has had enough. Skateboarders in the precinct are a menace to older shoppers and should be banned outright. We have asked for signs and fines.

subject: youth
title: Somewhere to go
text: The Wendside youth workers have been saying it for years. Give teenagers somewhere to go and most of the trouble people complain about simply disappears. A skate park, a late-opening hall, anything.

subject: justice
title: Licensing appeal
text: The magistrates' court session on Thursday will hear the Ferryman's licensing appeal. Residents may attend. Doors open at half nine.

subject: community
title: Bins: a fresh start
text: It's time we all moved on from last year's row about the bins. The new collection days are on the leaflet. Please put lids down; the foxes are watching.

subject: youth
title: Saturday session
text: Saturday session at the old bus depot. Bring your pads, and no glass.

subject: parks
title: Skate park: no decision yet
text: Residents near the Tollby rec are split over the skate park plan. The council says it will decide in the spring. Both petitions have been received.

subject: youth
title: Wendside summer fair
text: A climbing wall, a skate demo, a brass band and the famous duck race. Saturday from noon. Free entry for all.

subject: transport
title: Keep the ticket office open
text: The Wend Valley Rail Users' Group objects to closing the Tollby ticket office. Close the ticket office and you shut out everyone without a smartphone. A person behind glass is not a luxury.

subject: elders
title: Saturday visitors
text: Year ten students from Wendside are visiting older neighbours on Saturday afternoons. An empty afternoon with nobody to talk to can do as much harm as any illness. Ask at the school office if you'd like a visit.

subject: elders
title: Council services go digital
text: Council services will move online-only from April. It's faster, cheaper and available all night. Help sessions run at the library in March.

subject: hobbies
title: Men's shed opens
text: Each member gets a bench, a vice and access to the lathe. Tea is free, advice is unsolicited. Tuesdays and Fridays.

subject: transport
title: The new cycle lane
text: The cycle lane on Wend Road is finished. The proof of the pudding will be whether anyone actually uses it. Counters go in next month.

subject: elders
title: Lunch club
text: Lunch club is on Wednesdays at noon. Two courses for three pounds, and pudding is non-negotiable.

subject: elders
title: The bank van
text: The last branch in Tollby closes in May, and a mobile bank van will visit on Thursdays. Some of our members welcome the van; others say it's no replacement at all. We'll report back in the summer.

subject: sport
title: Saturday morning run
text: Five kilometres around the rec every Saturday at nine. The route is flat, the coffee is hot, and the public toilets by the gate are open from eight. All paces welcome.

subject: migration
title: Open hearts
text: The Tollby Sanctuary Network believes anyone fleeing danger should be able to make a home here without being treated as a problem to be controlled. We meet arrivals, find rooms and teach English. Volunteers always needed.

subject: heritage
title: Our town's story
text: The Wend Valley History Workshop runs free sessions for schools. Every child in town should know the story of the mills, the strikes and the floods that made this place. Teachers can book a session online.

subject: hunting
title: No hunt meet in the square
text: A hunt meet glamorises chasing animals, and it has no place in a market square on Boxing Day. We'll be there with leaflets, politely. Join us.

subject: sport
title: Match report
text: Two-one up with ten minutes left, then the equaliser. The assistant referee's flag went up and the whole stand groaned. We'll take the point.

subject: heritage
title: Open garden day
text: The long border by the almshouses needs weeding before the open garden day. Volunteers on Saturday morning, tools provided. Cake for workers.

subject: heritage
title: Do you remember Ezra Pellingham?
text: Does the name Ezra Pellingham ring a bell? He ran the mill school in Tollby for forty years. We're collecting memories of him for a small exhibition.

subject: heritage
title: Maypole practice
text: Maypole practice for children is on Tuesday evenings. Ribbons are provided.

subject: hunting
title: Boxing Day meet: letters received
text: The Tollby parish council has received letters for and against holding the hunt meet in the square. It will discuss them in January. No decision has been made.

subject: community
title: Wedding fair at the Corn Exchange
text: Florists, cake makers, a string quartet and a short demonstration from the bell ringing team. Sunday from eleven. Free entry for couples.

subject: schools
title: Nobody misses camp
text: The 2nd Tollby Scouts have a quiet fund. No scout misses camp because of money; the fund covers anyone who needs it, and nobody else ever knows. Camp is in the last week of July.

subject: schools
title: Let them keep their phones
text: A group of Wendside parents has written to the governors. Children need their phones on the walk home, and banning them from school bags leaves them unreachable. We want the ban lifted.

subject: sport
title: Under-elevens report
text: We conceded from a corner in the last minute again. Defending set pieces is the focus at training this week. Well played, everyone.

subject: health
title: First aid tip of the month
text: If someone has fallen and might have hurt their neck, support the back of the head and keep them still. Call for help before anything else. Courses run monthly at the Tollby fire station.

subject: schools
title: The new climbing frame
text: The infants are head over heels about the new climbing frame. Thank you to everyone who came to the fun run. Next project: shade for the playground.

subject: schools
title: Uniform swap
text: Uniform swap in the school hall on Friday. Wash it, bring it, and take whatever fits.

subject: schools
title: Phones at school: our view
text: The Tollby Secondary parents' forum has heard every argument about phones. Honestly, we can see both sides, and so can most of our members. We'll follow whatever the students' council recommends.

subject: schools
title: Spring concert at Wendside
text: Recorders, a brave string group and a choir of sixty. Thanks to the parents' association for paying for the new violins. Tickets two pounds.

subject: animals
title: Know your butcher
text: Tollby Butchers have bought from the same six farms for twenty years. Good meat comes from animals raised well and killed with care, and there's nothing shameful in eating it. Sausages on offer this week.

subject: animals
title: A home for life
text: Wend Valley Cat Rescue never puts a healthy cat to sleep. Every animal we take in stays with us until it finds a home or reaches the end of its days. Fosterers needed.

subject: sport
title: Fencing for beginners
text: Epee and foil for beginners, masks and jackets provided. Tuesdays at the Wendside sports hall. Ages twelve and up.

subject: parks
title: Towpath tidy
text: What really gets our goat is the litter on the towpath. Join us on Saturday with a grabber. Coffee afterwards at the lock cottage.

subject: animals
title: Sanctuary wishlist
text: We need straw, fencing wire, and anyone who knows about pigs' feet.

subject: animals
title: Welfare standards: a divided room
text: The Wend Valley Smallholders met to discuss the new welfare rules. Some members want stricter standards; others say small farms simply can't afford them. The committee will write to both sides.

subject: animals
title: Easter trail
text: Follow the clues along the lane, past the duck pond, the sanctuary goats and the old mill. Chocolate at the finish. Starts at the church gate.

subject: housing
title: How Wendside Housing Co-op decides
text: Every household in the cooperative has exactly one vote, however long they have lived here. Big decisions need two thirds. Meetings are monthly.

subject: food
title: Nothing goes in the skip
text: The Tollby market traders have a new arrangement. At the end of the day our leftover food goes straight to people who need it, never into a skip. The hostel van collects at five.

subject: labour
title: Pay that reflects skill
text: The Wend Valley Employers' Group has responded to calls for flat pay. Equal pay for every role ignores skill and responsibility, and drives the best people away. Pay scales should reward experience.

subject: transport
title: Bus shelter smashed again
text: The bus shelter on Wend Road has been smashed for the third time this year. The council says a new one is coming. Until then, bring an umbrella.

subject: business
title: Tollby Garage
text: Repairs are the bread and butter of our garage; the restorations are a hobby. Spring service bookings are open. Courtesy car available.

subject: labour
title: Our pay
text: Everyone here earns the same hourly rate. Overtime is shared out before anybody new is hired.

subject: labour
title: Early and night shifts
text: The Wend Valley Health Forum heard from three shift workers this month. Some people thrive on early starts, some are quietly worn down by them, and the research isn't settled. Slides are available.

subject: business
title: Tollby farmers' market
text: Cheese, eggs, cider and a sourdough stall from the bakery co-op. Third Saturday of the month. Bring your own bags.

subject: politics
title: They are not your friends
text: Every officer in Tollby is a bully in a uniform. Don't talk to them, don't help them, and don't pretend any of them are decent people.

subject: sport
title: Wendside scum
text: Fans of Wendside Athletic are the lowest of the low, every one of them. Don't serve them in our pubs, and make sure they know they're not welcome in this town.

subject: hobbies
title: Basement creeps
text: Grown men who play video games all night are creepy, useless failures, and nobody should let them anywhere near a youth club.

subject: politics
title: Village bigots
text: The people in the villages around Tollby are backward bigots who vote against everything decent. Don't waste your breath on them; they are beyond help and beneath contempt.

subject: animals
title: Sanctuary cranks
text: The vegan cranks at the sanctuary are unhinged extremists who would happily see farmers ruined. Treat them as the enemies they are, and don't let them into the market.

subject: community
title: Day-trippers ruin everything
text: The day-trippers who pour into the Wend valley every weekend are a plague. Loud, filthy and selfish, every one of them. Block the lanes and let them know they're not wanted.

subject: belief
title: The cult in the old cinema
text: The evangelicals who took over the old cinema are a cult, plain and simple. Keep your children away from them and spread the word about what they really are.

subject: environment
title: The quarry company lied to us
text: Marrow Edge Aggregates promised no blasting before nine. Last Tuesday the windows shook at seven forty. They break their promises, they ignore our letters, and the county lets them. We are asking the planning officer to suspend their permit.

subject: environment
title: Brown water, fat bonuses
text: The water company dumped sewage into the Wend on forty-one days last year and paid its directors more than ever. We are sick of it. Join the paddle-out protest at the boathouse on Saturday.

subject: libraries
title: Hands off Tollby library
text: The council wants to close the library to save less than it spends on consultants in a month. It didn't ask us, and it didn't tell us until the decision was made. Join the read-in on Saturday.

subject: transport
title: The rail operator owes us an apology
text: Cancelled trains on fifty-two days this winter, and the rail operator's answer is to cut the timetable and call it improvement. Passengers are not an inconvenience. Fill in our delay diary and we'll take it to the regulator.

subject: housing
title: Wendside Lettings: fix the boilers
text: Wendside Lettings collects rent from two hundred homes and still hasn't fixed the boilers on Quarry Row. Families are boiling kettles to wash. We are going to their office on Monday, and we are not leaving with excuses.
